areasHintText: Configure the daily opening/closing schedule per plan here. Pick a schedule mode: "All days the same" (a single open/close pair), "Weekday / weekend / public holiday" (the classic three-field schedule), or "Individual weekday + public holiday" (a separate open/close pair for each weekday, plus a public holiday override). Only the fields relevant to the selected mode are shown. Each open/close field is either a plain clock time ("HH:MM", 24h), an offset relative to sunrise (open) / sunset (close) written with a leading "+" (after) or "-" (before) sign as plain minutes (e.g. "-30") or an "HH:MM" duration (e.g. "+01:30") - append "d" (e.g. "-30d") to use civil dawn/dusk instead of the actual sunrise/sunset - or that offset combined with a "!HH:MM" cap time, e.g. "+30!19:00" (30 minutes after sunset, but never later than 19:00 - analogous for opening/sunrise). Leave a field empty to skip that action. Assign a plan to a covering on the Coverings tab.
groupsHintText: Combine configured coverings for joint control. Select all members of the group below.
heatingPeriodStart: Heating period start (MM-DD, e.g. 10-15) - fallback if summer state ID above is empty
holidayHintText: ID of an existing boolean state (own or foreign, e.g. from a calendar/iCal adapter) whose current value decides whether "today" counts as a public holiday for every plan below. true = public holiday, false/empty = not a public holiday. Leave empty to disable holiday-specific schedules entirely.
icalHintText: Optionally override a single day's opening/closing time via an `ioBroker.ical` instance (configure the actual calendar URL/file there, not here). Add an event whose title starts with the prefix above, e.g. "Rolläden auf 07:00" (overrides today's opening time for every plan) or "Rolläden: Kinderzimmer auf 07:00" (only for the plan named "Kinderzimmer"); use "zu" instead of "auf" to override the closing time. Leave the instance field empty to disable this entirely.
name: Name
notifyHintText: Optionally send a notification via an existing `pushover`/`telegram` adapter instance (e.g. "pushover.0") when a covering's watchdog reports it is not responding, or when storm/frost protection engages or clears for at least one covering (one combined notification, not one per covering). Configure the recipient/chat directly on that instance, not here. Both fields can be left empty to disable notifications entirely; either or both can be set at once.
orientationToleranceMinusDeg: Sun window tolerance, lower bound (°, relative to orientation)
orientationToleranceNoLocationHint: Corresponding time unknown (no location configured in system.config).
orientationToleranceNoTimeHint: Corresponding time: sun does not reach today's azimuth window at this orientation.
orientationTolerancePlusDeg: Sun window tolerance, upper bound (°, relative to orientation)
perWeekdayHintText: Set the open/close value for each individual weekday. Leave a field empty to skip that action on that weekday. The public holiday fields below apply on public holidays instead, falling back to the current weekday's value if left empty.
pickerHintText: Type at least 2 characters to search by ID or name, or browse the folder tree below.
scanHintText: Scans connected adapter instances for foreign states with a covering-related role and presents every newly found covering below as a preview (already configured coverings are never proposed again). Homematic (including the "Verschluss" enum.functions Gewerk), KNX, Shelly, Zigbee and Zigbee2MQTT are detected with their matching system; everything else falls back to the generic drivers. Review/rename the candidates and uncheck any you do not want, then confirm - only then are they actually added, which changes the adapter configuration and restarts the adapter instance automatically.
scenesHintText: Named presets that drive one or more coverings to specific positions at once. Position values use 0% = fully open/raised and 100% = fully closed/lowered. Add one target row for each covering.
shuttersHintText: Configure your roller shutters, blinds and awnings here. Each card represents one covering; only the fields relevant to its selected system and enabled protection functions are shown.
statePosition: Position command state ID (0% open/raised; 100% closed/lowered)
statePositionActual: Actual position state ID (0% open/raised; 100% closed/lowered)
statePositionActualInverted: Actual position state ID (0% closed/lowered; 100% open/raised)
statePositionInverted: Position command state ID (0% closed/lowered; 100% open/raised)
sunProtectionCloudCoverTriggerEnabled: Trigger sun protection by cloud cover alone
sunProtectionHintText: When "Orientation" above is set, the sun-window (when sun protection may apply) is derived from it: active whenever the current sun azimuth is within the tolerance below on either side of the orientation, e.g. a south-facing window (180°) with the default 70° tolerance is active for sun azimuths 110-250°. The window additionally requires the sun elevation to reach the minimum below (default 0° = above the horizon), and, if a maximum cloud cover is set, the sky to be clear enough (requires the cloud-cover state ID under Weather data). The sun window start/end fields are only used as a fallback when no orientation is set.
sunProtectionMaxCloudCoverPercent: Sun window: maximum cloud cover (%, empty = ignore)
sunProtectionMinElevationDeg: Sun window: minimum sun elevation (°, default 0)
sunWindowEnd: Sun window end (fallback, no orientation set)
sunWindowStart: Sun window start (fallback, no orientation set)
thresholdsHintText: Higher "close" thresholds mean the corresponding protection only reacts to stronger sun/wind, i.e. it activates less often. "Sun close/open" (W/m²) control sun protection (6.1): close activates it, open (lower, held for 10 minutes to avoid flickering when clouds pass) deactivates it again. "Trigger sun protection by cloud cover alone" is an optional addition (6.3, requires the cloud-cover state ID under Weather data): while enabled, sun protection also activates whenever cloud cover is at/below the "clear/mostly clear sky" percentage below, independent of the radiation reading - useful if radiation alone reacts too slowly or a sensor is unreliable. "Wind open/close-allowed" (km/h) work the same way for storm protection (7a): "open" is the speed storm protection engages at, "close-allowed" (lower, held for 10 minutes) is the calmer speed it must drop back below before normal operation resumes. "Frost threshold" (°C) is the outdoor temperature at/below which automated movement pauses if it is also damp/raining (7b). The night-cooling fields (7c) only apply to coverings with that feature explicitly enabled: the indoor temperature must reach the minimum, and be at least the configured amount warmer than outdoors, before a covering is kept open overnight instead of closing on schedule.
weatherHintText: Configure the foreign state IDs of your own weather station here. Any value left empty disables the protection functions that need it (an external weather-service fallback is not implemented yet). Cloud cover is optional and only used by the "trigger by cloud cover alone" option under Global thresholds. Wind direction is optional and only used by a covering's own "Rain: wind-direction tolerance" field (shown once rain protection is enabled and an orientation is set for that covering). "Summer" state ID left empty: sun protection instead uses the heating-period dates below (both empty too = always summer, the original default).
